maddeler.e: جَنْدَرَ • (jandara) Iq (non-past يُجَنْدِرُ (yujandiru), verbal noun جَنْدَرَة (jandara))
maddeler.t: By surface natively derived as from the root ج د ر (j d r). Maybe from Classical Persian جندر (jandar, “clothes”) or جندره (jandara, “calender, mangle; smoothening”) in the sense of giving a new look to something, as the present verb is said to specifically apply to garments or fabrics, and writing materials.
g: to restore, to reestablish, to renew the figure of
